sections.h2: Where Kent County deeds are recorded
sections.html:
The Register of Deeds is in the county Administration Building at 300 Monroe Avenue NW, in the middle of downtown Grand Rapids. Land contracts, liens and mortgages go through the same counter, under the Michigan Recording Act.

Staff will not supply blank deeds or advise on preparing one. Anyone changing the names on a deed can hire a real property attorney, use a title company or fill in a blank form. The office warns that forms pulled from the internet may fall short of recording rules.

Kent is a big county, with 675,232 people and 275,076 housing units. Owners occupy 70.3% of homes and the median home value is $289,900. Every parcel, from river valley city lots to rolling township acreage, is recorded at this one counter.

The base fee is $30 per document, in place since October 1, 2016. It covers deeds, mortgages, lis pendens notices and certified copies. These add-ons come up most often when a house changes hands:

  • Assignments or discharges covering several instruments add $3 per extra instrument, and the office asks you to limit these to 25 per document.
  • Deeds with a covenant of warranty, plus land contracts, need the treasurer's certification at $5 per deed (up to 25 parcels, 25 cents each beyond that). Write that check to the Kent County Treasurer, not the Register.
  • Copies are $1 per page. Searches start at $5, and certifying a document adds $5.
  • Pay with cash, a check or a money order. Make the check out to the Kent County Register of Deeds.

Electronic filers pay the statutory recording fee to the county, and an e-recording vendor can add its own processing fee on top.

The county rate is $1.10 and the state rate $7.50 per $1,000 of price, so every $1,000 carries $8.60. They come from Michigan's two transfer tax acts, MCL 207.504 and MCL 207.525.

Kent County transfer tax rates

County$1.10Seller

Combined$8.60Seller

The statute taxes each $500 or fraction of $500, so an odd price rounds the count up. Michigan has no transfer tax on mortgages.

The certification stamp comes from the Treasurer's Office, a separate counter from the Register of Deeds. It is one of the few transactions the treasurer still takes in person, at the first-floor counter of the Administration Building, weekdays 8 am to 5 pm.

Plan the order of events. A seller who learns at the last minute that taxes are open must first pay the treasurer, then collect the certification, and only after that bring the deed to the recording counter. The county's online delinquent tax search lets you check a parcel before you start, and the payment options page covers e-check, card, phone and mail payments for any balance.

sections.h2: Who owes the tax and how to claim an exemption
sections.html:
The seller, or grantor, owes it. Write the full price into the deed, or attach a Real Estate Transfer Valuation Affidavit. The affidavit carries no fee as long as the deed mentions it.

Exemptions must be written on the deed itself. The state's list in MCL 207.526 includes a parent deeding to a child or grandchild, foreclosure deeds, land contracts that have not yet passed title, and court orders that set no price. If land lies in two counties, state the price for each part.

sections.h2: Possible refund of the state tax
sections.html:
Some sellers can recover state transfer tax. The case is a seller who held a principal residence exemption and sold near the property's earlier assessed value. MCL 207.526(u) exempts a conveyance of property that carried the principal residence exemption when the state equalized value is no higher than the value set at the first tax day after the home was built or acquired, and the sale was an arm's-length price.

A refund claim needs the state refund application, copies of the recorded deeds showing the transfer tax stamp and proof of the sales price, and proof of the SEV from the local municipality. Copies of deeds come from the online deed search or from the office itself.

Approved e-recording vendors can file within a fixed window. Electronic documents are processed on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm, skipping county holidays, and the fee is collected by ACH through the vendors.

The county can reject any electronic filing that fails the Michigan Recording Act, and a party whose documents violate the state standards is cut off until further notice. It works with CSC eRecording, ePN, Simplifile and File and Go, and each vendor sets its own pricing. Recorded documents return to the submitter in electronic form. An individual seller will usually leave this step to the closing office.

sections.h2: Step by step for a seller
sections.html:
First, ask the closing office whether your deed carries a covenant of warranty. If it does, the treasurer's certification comes before anything else. Second, pay any open tax balance. Third, make sure the deed states the full price or has the valuation affidavit attached, and that any exemption is written on it.

Fourth, send the deed in. Most sellers let the title company e-record, but the counter at 300 Monroe Avenue NW takes paper too. Bring a check for $30 payable to the Kent County Register of Deeds, a second check for the treasurer's $5 certification, and the transfer tax. If a cash buyer is on the other side, the same steps apply, and the closing office usually handles them in one visit. Keep the receipt for your records.

Settle the property tax first, because the office cannot take a warranty deed without a treasurer's certificate. Under MCL 211.135 the certificate depends on a clean five-year tax record. Any open balance is settled by closing, and the Kent County Treasurer will quote it.

Check that the names on the deed match the owners of record. If a parcel's owner is unclear, ask Equalization or the local assessor for the tax roll name, which may differ from the true owner, then search recorded documents under it. After recording, the buyer has 45 days to give the local assessor the transfer notice under MCL 211.27a.

Ordering copies is simple. Visit in person, write a letter, or use the online document search. Copies cost $1 per page, certification is $5 per document, and a records search carries a $5 minimum.

faqs.q: What is the recording fee for a deed in Kent County?
faqs.a: Recording is $30 a document, under a schedule dated October 1, 2016. Budget a further $5 for the treasurer's tax certification on a warranty deed, plus any vendor charge if a filer submits electronically.

faqs.q: How high is the Kent County transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is $8.60 per $1,000 of price in total, split $1.10 county and $7.50 state. The seller owes it unless the deed states an exemption.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds help write a deed?
faqs.a: No. The office does not supply blank deeds or offer advice on preparing them. It sends people to an attorney, a title company or a blank form.

faqs.q: Will Kent County take a warranty deed while taxes are delinquent?
faqs.a: Not a warranty deed. State law requires a treasurer's certificate that taxes for the previous five years are paid. Quitclaim deeds with no warranty covenants are excepted.

faqs.q: How do I order a certified copy?
faqs.a: Visit the office in person, write a letter, or use the online document search. Copies cost $1 per page, certification is $5 per document, and a records search carries a $5 minimum.
